diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $v_1^2$, $v_2^2$ and $v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear, their sums $v_1^2 + v_2^2$, $v_1^2 + v_3^2$ and $v_2^2 + v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear too, which finalizes the proof of the lemma.
By Lemma \ref{le} vector $(\pm 1, 0)^T$ can be a right-singular vector of at most one of these three submatrices.

issues.failure_explanation: Take v_1=(1,0), v_2=(1,1), and v_3=(2,1). Their squares are (1,0), (0,2), and (3,4), which are pairwise non-collinear. However, the sums for pairs (1,2) and (2,3) are (1,2) and (3,6). More directly, the corresponding right Gram matrices are H=[[2,1],[1,1]] and [[5,3],[3,2]]=3H-I. They have identical ordered eigenvector directions, so both corresponding right-singular directions coincide, contrary to the lemma.

failure_location.quote: Then the three $2 \times 2$ matrices composed of these vectors as rows have pairwise different first (and second) right-singular vectors.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the lemma to assert that the three corresponding singular directions are not all identical. If they were identical, all three pair sums of squares would lie on one line; the identity 2v_i^2=(v_i^2+v_j^2)+(v_i^2+v_k^2)-(v_j^2+v_k^2) would then force all three squares onto that line. In Case A, use this weaker conclusion to select at least one submatrix whose minimum right-singular direction differs from (±1,0), rather than asserting that at most one submatrix can match it.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false, and its invocation does not justify the stated selection of submatrices in Case A. This leaves the strictness argument, and hence the equality characterizations in the proposition and corollary, without the given justification. The non-strict existence bound does not rely on this lemma.
issues.title: Non-collinear squares do not imply pairwise distinct singular directions
issues.why_classification: The stated auxiliary guarantee must be weakened, so this is not merely a typographical correction. A contained replacement argument and adjustment of its use suffice, while preserving the main equality characterization and its advertised regime.
